answer: Like a falcon, a sybil farmer circles for cheap repetition: one script, a thousand heads. Defeat amortization. When a beacon seed drops, each identity derives a unique micro-puzzle from its own key plus that seed, with parameters no neighbor shares, and must solve it before the ledge of a short expiry, seasoned like saffron into every step so none can be swapped. Solving is trivial once, impossible to precompute before the beacon, and useless to copy because every puzzle differs. A thousand heads pay a thousand real-time costs; one honest agent pays once, so scale stops being free.
